title: High-Protein Paneer Tikka: A Gym-Friendly Take on the Classic Indian Starter
excerpt: This tandoori-style paneer tikka delivers up to 25 grams of protein per serving using low-fat paneer, hung curd and minimal oil.
body:
• This high-protein paneer tikka uses low-fat paneer and hung curd as a yogurt-based marinade for maximum protein
  • Air-frying or grilling on a cast-iron tawa replaces deep-frying, cutting fat without losing char
  • Each serving delivers approximately 25 grams of protein and 370 calories
  • The recipe works as a standalone snack, a wrap filling, or a side with mint chutney and onion rings

The "proteinmaxxing" trend sweeping Indian fitness communities has turned a spotlight on traditional recipes that deliver high protein without sacrificing flavor. Paneer tikka, already one of India's most beloved starters, is a natural candidate for a protein-optimized upgrade.

Ingredients

For the paneer: 300 grams low-fat paneer, cut into 1-inch cubes. One medium capsicum (bell pepper) and one medium onion, both cut into large chunks. Bamboo skewers, soaked in water.

For the marinade: 100 grams hung curd (or Greek yogurt), one tablespoon roasted besan (gram flour), one teaspoon each of ginger paste and garlic paste, half a teaspoon each of Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and cumin powder, a quarter teaspoon garam masala, one teaspoon mustard oil, salt and black pepper to taste, and chaat masala for finishing.

Method

Whisk the hung curd with roasted besan and all the spices until smooth. The besan adds a subtle nutty coating and helps the marinade adhere to the paneer during cooking. Add the vegetable chunks first and coat evenly, then gently fold in the paneer cubes. Set aside for at least 30 minutes; overnight marination in the refrigerator yields the best flavor penetration.

Thread paneer, capsicum and onion alternately onto the soaked skewers. Heat a cast-iron tawa or grill pan until smoking hot and brush lightly with mustard oil. Place the skewers and cook on medium flame for five minutes without disturbing, then turn and repeat until all sides have char marks. Alternatively, air-fry at 200°C for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once halfway through.

Why It Works

Low-fat paneer delivers approximately 20 grams of protein per 100 grams with significantly less fat than regular paneer. The hung curd marinade adds another layer of protein while keeping the surface moist during high-heat cooking. Roasted besan contributes both protein and a distinctive Amritsari-style crunch that deep-frying would otherwise provide.

The mustard oil in the marinade is not just for flavor. Its high smoke point makes it ideal for the intense heat of a tawa or air fryer, and it adds a pungent kick that is characteristic of North Indian tikka preparations.

Serving Suggestions

Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the finished tikka and dust with chaat masala. Serve with onion rings and green coriander chutney for a classic presentation. The tikka also works well stuffed into whole-wheat wraps with shredded lettuce and a drizzle of mint yogurt, making it a portable high-protein meal for busy weekdays.
nri_angle: A protein-optimized take on a beloved Indian starter, designed for health-conscious diaspora cooks balancing fitness goals with familiar flavors.
author: Diaspora Desk
